newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Losses to Nafta share drive Slovak SAX index.
newsitem.headline: Losses to Nafta share drive Slovak SAX index.

text.p: Significant losses to Nafta drove the Slovak SAX index down 2.11 to 198.79 points in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday, with other blue chips closing mixed.

Brokers said the fall under the 200 point level had been expected and predicted that the SAX would stay flat in the near future, but from the long-term perspective the index should continue the downward trend.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta lost 200 crowns to close at 1,750, leaving brokers with mixed feelings over the future development in the price.

"Nafta's price is becoming interesting for investors, but the problem is that nobody seems willing to accept it and sell their holdings," said Libor Briska of Creditanstalt, adding, that the price should not continue to decline.
But Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said: "The story with Nafta is still the same, investors are very wary, and we expect the price to further decline."
Steel maker VSZ and oil refiner Slovnaft closed unchanged at 620 and 930 respectively, with brokers considering the two issues as undervalued.
"There is rather high interest to purchase Slovnaft shares, but, as it is with Nafta or VSZ, those who hold shares are not accept the price and resisting selling," Briska said.
Slovakia's largest commercial bank VUB lost 10 crowns to close at 1,650.
Overall volume fell to 259,591 shares traded, from 783,720 shares on Monday, the turnover decreased to 151.86 million crowns, from 152.17 million on Monday.
